evals.prompt: I changed the validation logic on the checkout page and want to add a reproducible check that can run in CI to confirm an empty cart cannot be submitted.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger frontend-verification. The result should first define the UI surface and the user-visible success criteria, then choose Playwright for reproducible assertions and regression coverage to match the intent, rather than only doing a one-off manual look.

evals.prompt: This page's initial render feels a bit janky. Help me take a one-off look at the layout shift and Core Web Vitals; no need to write tests.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger frontend-verification. The result should choose Chrome DevTools for a one-off visual/layout diagnosis, performance trace, and Core Web Vitals, making clear this is an ad hoc investigation and not treating it as persistent regression coverage.

evals.prompt: Help me use the browser to log into the admin panel, go to the order detail page, and screenshot the status as evidence. Note that I already have a logged-in session.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger frontend-verification. The result should use a session-aware browser and deliberately preserve the authenticated context, not assume a fresh isolated browser comes with cookies/profile/permissions; if the browser cannot start or attach, it should report the tool failure first before considering a fallback.

evals.prompt: I built an interactive HTML dashboard to send to the team. Help me confirm it works properly.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger frontend-verification. The result should load the rendered artifact, check for console errors, key elements and interactions, scalable text, hit areas, and modal/focus accessibility, and capture a canonical screenshot; it should also match the online/offline dependency strategy to the runtime environment.

evals.prompt: Help me design a Playwright page object model, choose locators, set up fixtures, and debug a flaky timeout in an existing spec.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger frontend-verification as the primary skill; designing a full Page Object Model and fixtures and debugging a spec is test-suite implementation that belongs to the project's native Playwright guidance. frontend-verification owns only the verification-strategy decision plus the durable Playwright core in references/playwright-essentials.md (locators, web-first assertions, flaky triage), unless the request also needs UI evidence or a broader verification-strategy decision.

evals.prompt: Help me optimize the performance of this backend-only SQL aggregation query; there are no frontend changes at all.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger frontend-verification; this is a pure backend/data-layer change that does not involve UI, the browser, or any renderable artifact.

evals.prompt: Help me write a plain-text weekly project report on this iteration's progress.
evals.expected_output: Should NOT trigger frontend-verification; this is reader-facing plain-text writing with no UI or HTML deliverable that needs verification in a browser.

evals.prompt: This page is behind a login with an image captcha. Help me drive the browser to solve the captcha and log in so I can screenshot the result as evidence.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger frontend-verification. Before hand-rolling captcha-solving or the login flow in the browser tool, the result should first search the project for an existing tested login/verification harness or helper (zero-touch auth entry, slider/image-captcha solver, MFA/TOTP) and reuse it, hand-driving the browser only when no such helper exists; it should preserve the authenticated context deliberately and stop per the stop condition if it begins hand-implementing a login or captcha flow while the project already ships one.

evals.prompt: I need to confirm this marketing landing page renders correctly across mobile, tablet, and desktop breakpoints. Help me verify the responsive layout.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger frontend-verification. The result should define the target viewports/breakpoints and per-viewport user-visible success criteria as the UI surface, then choose the browser tool by intent — Chrome DevTools device emulation for a one-off visual and layout-shift look at each breakpoint, or Playwright with explicit viewport sizes for reproducible, CI-stable responsive assertions — and capture a canonical screenshot per breakpoint rather than a single desktop-only view. If the responsive layout is a durable user-visible surface it should back the check with the smallest relevant Playwright test per references/playwright-essentials.md, not treat the ad hoc look as regression coverage.

evals.prompt: 样式改完了,帮我在浏览器里把下单流程从头到尾点一遍,确认页面没有坏。
evals.expected_output: Should trigger frontend-verification from Chinese-language phrasing. The result should define user-visible success criteria for the checkout flow, drive it in a real browser, and capture evidence of the final state rather than declaring success from code changes alone.
